# Code style

- STY-001: Follow the Microsoft .editorconfig baseline at the repo root; every rule it adopts is a warning (STY-004 makes warnings fail the build).
- STY-007: Naming: by convention, C# programs use PascalCase for type names, namespaces and all public members; use camelCase for method parameters and local variables, and the s_ prefix for private and internal static fields (STY-014 changes this for static readonly and thread-static fields); use the Async suffix for methods that return awaitable types, which doesn't necessarily apply to methods your code doesn't call explicitly, such as event handlers or web controller methods; use meaningful and descriptive names for variables, methods and classes; avoid abbreviations and acronyms in names, except widely known and accepted abbreviations; avoid single-letter names, except simple loop counters; and identifiers shouldn't contain two consecutive underscores. For code: use the using syntax that doesn't need braces, collection expressions to initialize collection types, a concise form of new when the variable type matches the object type, parentheses to make clauses in an expression apparent, a dedicated System.Threading.Lock as the lock object of a lock statement (in .NET 9 and C# 13 or later), && and || instead of & and | in comparisons, Func and Action instead of defining delegate types, a lambda for an event handler you don't need to remove later, int rather than unsigned types, string interpolation to concatenate short strings, a StringBuilder to append strings in loops, required properties instead of constructors to force initialization, static members called through the class name, and meaningful names for query variables; prefer raw string literals to escape sequences or verbatim strings. For layout: one statement and one declaration per line, at least one blank line between method and property definitions, and comments on a separate line, beginning with an uppercase letter and ending with a period.
- STY-014: Where the kit departs from STY-007's pages: a static readonly field that isn't private takes PascalCase, not s_ (Microsoft's field naming guidelines give a public static field PascalCase and no prefix; the identifier names page gives an internal static field s_, which CA1707, checking internal APIs here, fails as an underscore); a thread-static field takes s_, not t_ (a naming rule can't tell a field by its [ThreadStatic] attribute); a constructor that only assigns its parameters is a primary constructor (IDE0290); and an Async suffix isn't required on an event handler, a controller action (MVC trims the suffix, so nameof() in CreatedAtAction would name a missing action), middleware's Invoke or a test method (ADR-0076: a naming rule tripped these, so the owner's decision keeps the suffix advisory).
